category_title: Minimally verbal young children with severe ASD and language processing deficits
minimal_context: The student is working one-on-one with a therapist to imitate vowel sounds using picture cards and bubbles.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Look at this picture card. Say /a/.

STUDENT: (Looks at the drawing of the vocal shape on the picture card but does not produce any meaningful vocalizations or words.)

TUTOR: Let's try another one. Say /i/.

STUDENT: (Remains silent, failing to imitate the vocalization of the chosen sound.)

TUTOR: I have some bubbles here. Say /u/.

STUDENT: (Shows a reduced response to the task, continuing to not imitate the adult's model despite the pictorial cues and bubble activity.)

options.A: Maintain an adult-to-child ratio of 1:2 to 1:4, or if working one-on-one, nominate one more peer to join the speech and language training.
options.B: Adopt the same sequence of learning activities in each session, using a sticker-system for reinforcement during the speech and language training.
options.C: Implement a specific 'Termination' stage, counting down the final 3-5 sessions of the speech and language training program with the student.
options.D: Implement alternative communicative modes, such as a picture communication system, to bridge her communicative needs while continuously prompting her to express verbally.
